section_summary.extract_value: This Introduction reviews the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) as a widely used measure of positive body image, summarizes evidence for its convergent and cross-cultural validity, and highlights that the BAS often shows a one-dimensional structure in Western samples but can exhibit a two-factor structure in some non-Western samples. The section notes implications for using translated BAS versions and cautions against assuming unidimensionality across cultures.
section_summary.evidence_source: One of the most widely used measures of positive body image is the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS; Avalos, Tylka, & Wood-Barcalow, 2005), a 13-item measure that taps into four qualities of positive body image, namely holding positive opinions of the body, acceptance of the body despite its imperfections, respect for the body, and protection of the body through the rejection of unrealistic ideals. Broadly speaking, these studies suggest that three items on the BAS may be distinguishable from the construct of body appreciation among some non-Western populations.
